Hey! If you're new here, I'm posting some old facts I wrote for non-railroaders. Feel free to correct anything you see as wrong.

What? NASA and trains? WTF is this? Yes sir, NASA has it's very own railroad. If you've even been to Cape Canaveral, you've probably seen its tracks or even a train.

NASA is a Class III railroad, meaning it's super small. And it is: with only 40miles of track on Cape Canaveral and in Titusville, Florida. Originally, NASA borrowed three ALCO S2s from the Army. These were used to carry construction supplies to the Cape during construction. Over time the railroad began to lose use as less and less building occurred. Then along came the space shuttle. A means of transportation was needed to transport the new Solid Rocket Boosters from their factory in Utah. They were too big for trucks (duh). So hey, why not use that old railroad? Unfortunately, Florida climate had gotten the better of the railroad. So they spent money to upgrade it! Concrete ties and thermite joints meant a super heavy and low maintenance railroad. New locomotives were needed, too. In 1983, NASA bought 3 SW1500 locomotives. Painted dull red and grey (similar to the "worm" logo color scheme), these trains served as the official SRB haulers for NASA. Here's how it worked:

At the end of the NASA line in Titusville, there's a small yard (it used to be bigger but the track upgrades made it smaller). The local Class II railroad, the Florida East Coast RR, drops off the SRB consist (which travels from UP to CSX to NS then to FEC), and then runs away like a scared child before the NASA monster comes out. A NASA SW unit will come and pick up the SRB train and then haul it to the shuttle assembly building. Then it will drop off the cars at the locomotive maintenance center and sleep. After STS-XXX launches, the SRBs are recovered, cleaned, and then put on the special cars again. Then the processes is reversed, and starts all over.

Oh yeah, I forgot to mention that NASA has special cars. NASA has special cars. Derived from flatcars, they have brackets that enable them to carry segments of the SRBs. In between each of these cars is a yellow spacer boxcar. While these empty cars may seem like they're there to cushion crashes, they're actually there to keep the weight of the train even as it crosses the bridge from Florida to Cape Canaveral.

NASA's railroad crew, known as URS, is a small club of dedicated guys. To them, these 3 SW switches and the fleet of 100 or so cars are their pride and joy. They recently repainted #3 to represent a more modern NASA, with blue and white being the main two colors. They often make their own freight cars from scratch to meet whatever needs their cargo requires, such as the SRB cars or Titan III missile cars. They also contract out to those freaks on the lower end of the Cape, the USAF. These guys have been so dedicated to keeping everything running smoothly that there hasn't been an accident on the railroad for 30 years, aka since it's opening.

Sadly, with the closure of the shuttle program, the NASA railroad has lost basically all of its business. What does this mean? Recently most of the equipment has been sold off or donated, and the tracks are now empty. SpaceX's lease of the old shuttle launch pad probably means some trackage will be removed.
